title: Adding CSS to a page
summary: Style a page with an inline style and with a style element, and read the shape of a CSS rule.

quiz.q: Which part of a CSS rule says **what** to style?
quiz.explain: The selector (for example `p`) picks the elements. The declarations inside the braces say how to style them.

quiz.q: Complete the rule so every paragraph becomes green.
quiz.explain: `color` sets the text colour. A declaration is `property: value;`.

quiz.q: You want one stylesheet shared by ten pages. What is the best way?
options: Copy a style element into every page
Put the rules in a .css file and link it from each page
Write the rules in the body
quiz.explain: A separate .css file, loaded with `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`, is written once and reused by every page.

quiz.q: Click the line with the mistake.
quiz.explain: Every declaration ends with a semicolon. Without it the browser cannot see where `color: red` stops, so it ignores both lines.

exercise.task:
Style the page in two ways. Work in `index.html`.

- Give the `<h1>` an inline `style` attribute that makes its colour red.
- In the `<style>` element write a rule for `p` that makes paragraph text blue and `font-size` 18px.
hints: An inline style is an attribute on the tag itself, for example `<h1 style="...">`.
Inside the style element write `p { ... }` and put two declarations between the braces, each ending with a semicolon.

Welcome

/* inside the style element */ p { color: blue; font-size: 18px; }

checks.name: The h1 has an inline style attribute
checks.hint: Add style="..." to the opening h1 tag.

checks.name: The h1 text is red
checks.hint: Write color: red; inside the inline style.

checks.name: Paragraph text is blue
checks.hint: In the style element add p { color: blue; }.

checks.name: Paragraph font size is 18px
checks.hint: Add font-size: 18px; to the p rule.

checks.name: The rule is written in a style element
checks.hint: Write the p rule between <style> and </style>.
